transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (Mirador - Head of ML), Ben Cho (Mirador - Platform), Samir Patel (CTO), Lina Gomez (Compliance)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through SLO proposals and measurement plan. Customer asked about VPC/on-prem constraints, data retention, and how to measure TTFT vs TPOT under bursty traffic. Agreed on hybrid SLO weighting and next steps to exchange traces and run benchmark harness.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this tight, goal is to pick SLOs and the measurement plan for the pilot.
[00:25] Marta Alvarez: Thanks Alex, quick context — Mirador's chat assistant is live in beta, about 10k active users/day, spikey during morning triage. We need predictability more than yesterday's new features.
[00:45] Ben Cho: Our platform stack is EKS, private subnets, we want VPC peering if possible; also curious on dedicated vs hosted options; security is top requirement.
[01:12] Priya Nair: Great. For the pilot we usually recommend TTFT and TPOT metrics — time to first token (TTFT) for perceived latency and time per token (TPOT) for sustained throughput cost. We'll propose p95/p99 bands.
[01:35] Samir Patel: Quick question — should we pick one or both? The team worries about per-token cost impact if we only optimize TTFT.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Good point. We've been doing a hybrid acceptance before: primary gate on TTFT p95 during traffic bursts and a secondary TPOT p99 threshold to control tail-costs. That avoids regressing tail latency when you micro-opt for first token.
[02:38] Marta Alvarez: Can you quantify with numbers? Our internal threshold is users drop off if first response > 400ms.
[03:00] Priya Nair: From similar pilots, for a 7B-class llama-style model shipped on mid-tier GPUs, a reasonable starting proposal: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 550ms, TPOT p95 <= 28ms/token, TPOT p99 <= 75ms/token. But we should adjust based on sequence length distribution — longer responses increase TPOT contribution.
[03:36] Ben Cho: Those TPOT numbers look... optimistic. Our median reply is 40 tokens with occasional 200 token reports. How does that affect the SLO?
[04:05] Priya Nair: Right — for medium length responses the TTFT dominates perceived latency. For long generation flows, TPOT multiplied by token count gives total tail time. We're recommending a weighted SLO: 70% weight on TTFT composite (p95) and 30% on TPOT tail (p99) for the acceptance gate. That matches product feedback studies.
[04:42] Marta Alvarez: That 70/30 makes sense, can we be explicit in acceptance criteria so legal/compliance can sign off?
[05:00] Lina Gomez: We need clear rollback criteria — e.g., if p99 TTFT increases by 2x for three consecutive days, automatic fallback to previous model. Also we need audit logs and SOS2 evidence. (sic)
[05:30] Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll include an acceptance matrix: baseline, target, and rollback thresholds plus required artifacts (bench logs, profiler traces, raw samples). We'll also provide SOC2 whitepaper and KMS integration notes.
[06:00] Jordan Li: Technical detail — our runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching; during the harness we'll enable/disable cache to measure cold vs warm starts. Recommend measuring TTFT both cold-first-request and warm (steady-state).
[06:30] Samir Patel: How do you define cold vs warm in the measurement?
[06:45] Priya Nair: Cold = empty KV cache for that keyspace and no affinity. Warm = after a realistic traffic ramp where caching is active. We'll run both: cold-run (10% of samples) and warm-run (90%).
[07:12] Marta Alvarez: On sampling — we can share 72 hours of anonymized traces. Are you good with CSV export?
[07:28] Alex Chen: Yes CSV is fine. Prefer fields: timestamp, endpoint, prompt length, response length, approximate user region. Redact PII.
[07:45] Ben Cho: Network — we need to know egress costs and whether Redwood Dedicated can sit inside our VPC.
[08:00] Alex Chen: We support private deployments (Redwood Private) which can be set up with VPC peering; we'll include network egress estimates in the cost attachment. Note 'Red wood' is sometimes misheard by our ASR, sorry — that came out weird in notes earlier.
[08:25] Samir Patel: (laughs) ASR aside, timeline question — how long for a full benchmark and acceptance?
[08:40] Priya Nair: Proposed timeline: week 1 scoping and exchange of traces, week 2 run orchestration and initial runs, week 3 analyze and tune (batching, quant), week 4 optional iteration / fine tuning and sign-off. So 3–4 weeks.
[09:05] Marta Alvarez: If tuning requires quantization and model variant tests, that could add cost/time. Do you run quantized variants automatically?
[09:20] Jordan Li: We can run 4 variants in parallel: full fp16, int8 quant, int8+KV cache, and a small-footprint trimmed model. That helps show tradeoffs for TTFT vs TPOT.
[09:45] Ben Cho: For measurement plan: what acceptance sample size do you recommend for p99 to be stable?
[10:00] Priya Nair: For p99 stability we usually target at least 50k samples overall with traffic stratified across sequence lengths and user regions. If your daily traffic is 10k active users, a 3-day window gives 30k; we ask for synthetic scaled runs to reach 50–100k in the harness.
[10:30] Marta Alvarez: Can Redwood produce synthetic traffic that respects our session distribution?
[10:40] Alex Chen: Yes we'll parameterize the harness to mimic session lengths and burst patterns; we'll share the generator config so you can validate.
[10:55] Lina Gomez: Security — will the harness store any prompts? Sensitive PII must not be persisted.
[11:10] Priya Nair: The default harness streams traces to memory and writes only aggregated metrics unless given explicit permission to persist raw prompts. We'll provide a scrubber step in the runbook.
[11:30] Samir Patel: On SLO numbers again — I'm worried p99 TPOT 75ms/token could blow cost. If you apply to long replies that skyrockets.
[11:50] Alex Chen: That's why we're keeping TPOT as a secondary gate and using weighted composition. Also run-level contract can cap cost by limiting tokens per request or setting fallback to smaller model after X tokens.
[12:15] Ben Cho: We should add a budget guardrail as an acceptance condition — e.g., 95th-percentile cost per request below $Y in the harness.
[12:35] Priya Nair: Agree. We'll include an economic guard in the acceptance matrix: unit-cost estimate measured on the benchmark run.
[12:50] Marta Alvarez: What about p95 vs p99 choice — you proposed p95 for TTFT and p99 for TPOT, why that split?
[13:05] Priya Nair: p95 captures the usual user experience for first token while p99 on TPOT captures tail behavior that can cause runaway cost on long sequences. Putting p99 on TPOT helps protect against worst-case per-token slowdown.
[13:30] Samir Patel: Okay makes sense. We still want to see p99 TTFT in monitoring, just not as the primary gate.
[13:42] Alex Chen: Yes we'll report both. Acceptance gate will assert TTFT p95 and TPOT p99, with p99 TTFT used in alerting and rollback criteria.
[14:00] Marta Alvarez: Let's capture specific numeric targets in the draft acceptance matrix so compliance can review.
[14:15] Alex Chen: Proposed starting numeric targets (draft): TTFT p95 <= 300ms, TTFT p99 <= 600ms (monitor only), TPOT p95 <= 35ms/token, TPOT p99 <= 80ms/token. Weighted acceptance score: 0.7*normalized(TTFT_p95_target) + 0.3*normalized(TPOT_p99_target) must be >= 0.9.
[14:50] Ben Cho: Normalized? Please include the exact formula in the doc.
[15:00] Priya Nair: We'll include calc formula and example. Also include the sample-size for each percentile and bootstrap method used to compute p99 confidence intervals.
[15:20] Marta Alvarez: For the benchmark run, can we test both hosted and dedicated variants? We want to see cost/perf delta.
[15:35] Jordan Li: Yes we'll run both where feasible; dedicated runs may show lower TTFT at similar TPOT depending on batching. We'll surface delta table.
[15:50] Samir Patel: Anything else on measurement — cold-start and warm-state samples, network variance, and region splits?
[16:05] Priya Nair: We'll include those in the run configs. Also recommend measuring tail under burstiness by running a 10x burst test to validate autoscale and queueing impacts.
[16:30] Ben Cho: On the orchestration side, we'll need an agreed run window to avoid impacting prod traffic — suggested off-hours like 02:00 UTC.
[16:45] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll coordinate run windows when scheduling.
[17:00] Marta Alvarez: If the benchmark shows we fail target, what is the typical remediation path?
[17:12] Alex Chen: Two paths: 1) Tuning (batching, cache, sequence truncation) within the pilot, or 2) fallback to a smaller model or different shard/instance until we iterate. Rollback criteria will be automatic if p99 TTFT > 2x baseline for 72 hours.
[17:35] Priya Nair: We'll also provide recommended quantization profile with expected delta numbers so you can trade cost vs quality.
[17:50] Lina Gomez: For compliance sign-off we'll need SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM notes.
[18:05] Alex Chen: We'll attach SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc to the runbook.
[18:20] Ben Cho: Anything on evaluation prompts? We'll want a short prompt set representing our top 100 intents.
[18:32] Marta Alvarez: Yep we'll send top-100 intents after redaction.
[18:45] Alex Chen: Great — recap of action items: Redwood shares harness + runbook; Mirador shares traces + top-100 prompts; schedule the runs. We'll produce a draft acceptance matrix and cost estimate within 48 hours after we get traces.
[19:10] Samir Patel: Sounds good. If we can get the harness early, we can run a small smoke test next week.
[19:25] Alex Chen: We'll aim to deliver harness by Oct 13.
[19:40] Marta Alvarez: Thanks all. Quick note — please make sure the draft has explicit rollback language the legal team can sign.
[19:55] Alex Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[20:10] [call ends]

Questions (auto):
- "How will cold vs warm cache be simulated?" -> Answered: cold 10% / warm 90% split in harness.
- "What sample size for stable p99?" -> Answered: aim 50k+ samples with stratified synthetic scaling if needed.
